newsitem.title: UK: Insurers want seat on Hong Kong legislature - pape.
newsitem.headline: Insurers want seat on Hong Kong legislature - pape.

text.p: Insurers will make a formal request to the Hong Kong Preparatory Committee this month for an independent insurance constituency seat in the first legislative council next year, according to the South China Morning Post.

The newspaper said the industry will lobby the committee, the Provisional Legislature and Xinhua (the New China News Agency), to win support for an independent voice for insurers, who are currently lumped together with stockbrokers, futures brokers and brokers of the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society in a constituency represented by legislator Chim Pui-chung.

It quoted Hong Kong Federation of Insurers chairman Steven Lau Hon-keung as saying: "Obviously the insurance industry is very different in nature to stockbrokers, futures brokers and gold dealers, and they should not be put together".

"The insurance industry does not receive enough attention from the legislator representing the current constituency, because there are fewer votes for insurance companies compared with stockbrokers," he said.
